payload.name: Preserve Direct Answers in Extraction
payload.description: When a speaker directly answers a question about how they learned or acquired a skill, include that answer as a distinct fact during extraction and keep it when updating an existing memory.
content: During extraction, list every discrete factual statement in a message; do not omit facts merely because they do not match the main theme of an existing memory.

When a message directly answers a question about how, when, or from whom the speaker learned a skill, always capture that answer (e.g., self-taught, taught by someone, learned at a certain age) as part of the candidate content.

When updating an existing memory, preserve all newly stated details in the enriched content or create an additional candidate; do not select just the facts that expand the current memory and drop the direct answer.

solves: Extraction candidates often keep only facts that align with an existing memory theme and silently drop other directly stated facts, such as how someone learned a skill (self-taught vs taught). This matters when a later question asks about that dropped fact. The Skill instructs extraction to capture every discrete fact from a message, especially direct answers to questions about acquisition or ability, and to preserve those facts when enriching an existing memory.
